Robots expose typed skill libraries with parameters, preconditions, costs and synchronization requirements; workflow contracts and runtime state are checked again at dispatch time, including state-bound values that cannot be known at planning time.

Evaluated on a drone-UGV Gazebo crew plus hardware-equivalent humanoid-quadruped workflows and two physical Unitree G1/Go2 trials.

Paper-linked GitHub repository returned 404 and exact repository search returned 0; no independent reproduction or cross-hardware serving evidence. Keep SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY / WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: ACSeL: Adaptive Configuration Search for Hardware-Constrained LLM Inference
papers.open_source: No author-linked public repository verified in the paper or exact GitHub repository search.

papers.key_results: Full text reports 13,618 RTX A6000 and 4,309 Jetson Thor latency measurements; evaluates vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM configurations under memory and latency constraints.
papers.maturity_note: Full official PDF inspected. Strong edge-serving configuration/profiling candidate, but it is an offline search/calibration framework rather than a runtime scheduler or serving abstraction. No author-linked public implementation verified; independent reproduction and deployment/fleet SLO remain open. Keep CORE_SYS / WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
papers.maturity_note: Evaluation is open-loop sensor replay, not closed-loop perception-control or online serving. Indoor scene coverage and generalization remain limited; no author-linked public repository or license was verified despite a release claim.

papers.title: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration
papers.maturity_note: No real-robot or model-serving evaluation. The matching repository has no root LICENSE, so redistribution/reuse terms are unresolved.

papers.title: Kinematic Hypothesis Context: Embodiment-Conditioned Learned Video Coding for Bandwidth-Limited Robot Policy Uplinks
papers.maturity_note: No author-linked public code or reproducible serving stack. The evidence is codec/uplink quality and policy success, not end-to-end serving p99, scheduler behavior or multi-robot goodput.

papers.title: Fast and Reliable Open-Vocabulary Object Search with Absence Detection from Robot Memory
papers.maturity_note: The 2 s live result is a single-robot, single-consumer-GPU pipeline, not a multi-tenant serving benchmark. No p99, admission control, fleet goodput, scheduler or public implementation was verified; the optional LLM path is about 10 s.

papers.title: Embodied RAG++: Retrieval-Augmented Generation From What Exists to What Works in Embodied Scenes
papers.maturity_note: The benchmark assumes object-to-manual links are known and is simulation-only; physical-robot validation under perception/localization noise is future work. The 15–20 s query-plus-generation path is not a low-latency serving runtime; no public implementation or p99/fleet SLO was verified.

papers.title: Time-Indexed Skill Success Models for Latency-Aware Skill Selection and Timing in Dynamic Manipulation
papers.maturity_note: A planning/competence model, not an inference-serving runtime. The real-robot study is narrow and does not measure multi-tenant serving or fleet SLO.

papers.title: Spatial-UMI-Dream: Scaling World Action Models with Metric Geometry for UMI Manipulation
papers.maturity_note: Policy success rates (79.10% in-domain, 72.15% under combined embodiment/environment shifts, 85.0% average across six real-world tasks) are task-success metrics, not serving throughput or latency. No inference-serving runtime, scheduling/cache mechanism, p99 or fleet SLO is established.

papers.title: Population-Scalable Multi-Agent World Modeling across Scene Geometries
papers.system_contribution: Khora separates a persistent shared world state (STBoard) from per-view diffusion rendering, with action-conditioned entity updates and a population-agnostic rendering interface. It includes an interactive runtime and measured population scaling.
papers.key_results: Measured 1–80 agents: compute-only rollout latency 107.16–116.73 ms and per-view FPS 37.33–34.27; end-to-end delivery latency 113.51–205.62 ms and per-view FPS 35.24–19.45; aggregate view throughput 37.3–2741.3 view-FPS. At 80 agents the deadline-fallback worker count reaches 53. Per-GPU VRAM remains nearly flat.
papers.maturity_note: One GPU per agent; no multi-tenant GPU sharing, admission control, fleet placement or serving SLO. The 128–1024-agent figures are compute-only projections, not measured end-to-end runs. Network/encoding/client delivery are excluded from those projections. No author-linked code repository found; project page/demo exist.

papers.title: EmboTeam: Asymmetric State Grounding for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Collaboration
papers.system_contribution: LLM-generated state expectations are verified through PDDL and grounded into a team-level parallel behavior tree. Robot-specific subtrees perform precondition checks, skill execution, effect validation, local replanning and blackboard-based synchronization.
papers.key_results: MACE-THOR: 42 heterogeneous multi-robot tasks across 8 indoor layouts. Abstract reports task success 12%→55% and goal-condition recall 32%→75%; fulltext shows task-family variation and a simulator-only evaluation.
papers.maturity_note: No real-robot deployment, no inference/serving latency or resource-sharing evaluation, and no author-linked repository found. Useful for planner/execution coordination, not a serving-system promotion.

papers.title: Visual-Redundancy-Controlled Parallel Decoding for Diffusion-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.system_contribution: Training-free inference-time token selection for diffusion MLLMs using a Visual Redundancy Index and token-to-image attention to select visually complementary positions in parallel.
papers.key_results: Relative accuracy gains up to 18.8% on M3CoT and 6.9% on MMBench. Fulltext throughput on L40 is 46.264 versus 46.982 tokens/s for the confidence baseline (about 1.5% throughput cost).
papers.maturity_note: Algorithmic decoding contribution; does not introduce serving admission/scheduling, model disaggregation or a runtime abstraction. Author-linked Apache-2.0 code and NeurIPS 2026 acceptance verified.

papers.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.system_contribution: WholeBodyMem uses SAM3-tracked object events to select a small adaptive set of pre-history frames, which the action expert reads with object/time tokens; HuMeGo adds six simulated and six real Unitree G1 tasks.
papers.key_results: Real G1: 53/60 successes (88.3%) versus 22/60 (36.7%) for the memoryless baseline; simulation 72.6% versus 29.1%.
papers.maturity_note: Memory/selection algorithm rather than serving runtime. No inference latency or online resource profile; SAM3 misses never-detected cues, online tracking adds inference cost, simulator demonstrations are scripted. Author-linked Apache-2.0 code found.

papers.title: Fast-VLA: You Only Think Once for Robot Manipulation
papers.system_contribution: A frozen 4B VLM is invoked once per episode to build a 34-layer KV task memory; a lightweight online actor retrieves from this fixed memory using live multi-view observations and robot state. The repository includes a policy server, evaluation clients, training code, first-frame cache builder and released checkpoints.
papers.key_results: RoboTwin 2.0: 92.46%/92.40% success, 92.43% mean, 1.437 ms amortized per environment step and 1.22 GiB post-prefill online memory; 10.9–17.1× lower inference time than three continually conditioned baselines. LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus: 95.95%/79.11%, 3.975 ms/step. 10,000 RoboTwin rollouts and 10,030 LIBERO-Plus perturbation instances.
papers.maturity_note: Peak prefill memory is 12.11 GiB (RoboTwin) and 11.74 GiB (LIBERO), much higher than post-prefill resident memory. Task memory is fixed for the episode; goal/instruction changes during execution are unaddressed. Strong state-reuse/online actor boundary candidate, not a multi-tenant serving system.

papers.title: MCUFlowNet: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Optical Flow on Microcontrollers
papers.system_contribution: PACE-NAS separates peak-SRAM design from latency search: platform profiling and backbone restructuring fix the memory peak, then a weight-sharing supernet and evolutionary Pareto search select operators and depths using accuracy and compiler-estimated latency for MCU optical flow.
papers.key_results: On Grove Vision AI V2 (Cortex-M55/Ethos-U55, INT8), peak SRAM is reduced by 18%; MCUFlowNet-S runs at 93.2 ms versus 164.3 ms for retrained EdgeFlowNet (1.76x faster), with EPE 6.50 versus 6.40 and simulated obstacle-avoidance success 51.5% versus 41.8% at 2 m/s. A balanced PIDNet-S variant is 1.17x faster at similar mIoU.
papers.maturity_note: Hardware-aware edge model optimization rather than a serving runtime. No serving scheduler, admission control, multi-tenant resource manager or serving SLO. The paper-linked GitLab main HEAD is reachable, but the web UI/raw files were inaccessible; license, CI, tests and reproduction scripts remain unverified.

papers.title: FastAFD: When Does Attention-FFN Disaggregation Pay on Rack-Scale NVLink?
papers.system_contribution: Open-source attention–FFN disaggregation engine for MoE inference on GB200 NVL72. It overlaps one microbatch's MoE expert computation with the next microbatch's attention and uses an analytical throughput model to decide when AFD beats colocated wide expert parallelism.
papers.key_results: The 24-page official PDF reports up to 1.17× throughput over the best tuned vLLM wide-EP setting on Qwen3 and 1.16× on Qwen3.5, matching on MiniMax-M2.5; the analytical model predicts throughput within 3% from colocated vLLM profiles. The repository README separately reports 1.35–1.45× against colocated baselines; these are different baselines and must not be conflated.
papers.maturity_note: Author-linked MIT repository includes benchmark scripts, correctness-alignment checks and CPU test coverage. The demonstrated environment is narrow (aarch64/CUDA 13.0 and an 8-GPU GB200 NVL72 cluster); no independent reproduction was run in this workspace and no VLM/Omni or Physical-AI transfer has been demonstrated. Track as a multimodal/omni-adjacent MoE serving CORE_SYS candidate, but keep WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: Phantom: Temporal Caching for Diffusion Models
papers.system_contribution: Algorithm–architecture co-designed diffusion accelerator that treats inter-step similarity as differential sparsity: a temporal cache reuses low-change activations while an outlier path recomputes high-magnitude differences at higher precision, with a streaming cache-update and sparse-computation pipeline.
papers.key_results: The 13-page official PDF reports average 4.0× speedup and 5.5× energy savings over GPUs and prior accelerators while preserving generation quality; the paper also reports about 22% area overhead for the proposed design.
papers.maturity_note: A hardware/algorithm boundary result for diffusion temporal reuse, not an online serving scheduler or multi-tenant runtime. No author-linked repository, license or independently reproducible artifact was found. Keep SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/WATCH_ONLY until an executable artifact and end-to-end serving integration are available.

papers.title: HyperVAttention: Efficient Sparse Attention with Spatio-Temporal Clustering for Video Diffusion
papers.system_contribution: 3D local-window clustering with custom Triton kernel, anchor-step full clustering plus intermediate subset updates, and hardware-aware CTA cluster merging; author repo provides Wan 2.2 and HunyuanVideo inference scripts with CTA-aware settings.
papers.key_results: Official abstract reports up to 2.13x speedup over full attention on HunyuanVideo and 2.23x for HVA-Flash, with higher fidelity than SVG2 at comparable latency.
papers.maturity_note: Video-diffusion sparse-attention/kernel optimization rather than a reusable serving runtime. No admission control, multi-tenant scheduler, fleet orchestration, serving SLO, LICENSE file, or test suite was verified. No independent reproduction; keep WATCH_ONLY and outside CORE_SYS.

papers.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
papers.system_contribution: Pre-registered audit of test-time candidate-selection signal, realized inference efficiency, and simulator/evaluation integrity for Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa; identifies silent rendering corruption and describes a detector/fix/scripts, but does not provide a serving scheduler or reusable runtime.
papers.key_results: Learned value selector is 1.66 percentage points worse than random; hindsight oracle +1.40 pp with episode-level interval spanning zero; 82% of states have identical candidate outcomes; token pruning yields at most 1.15x deployed end-to-end speedup (1.25x decode-excluded); adaptive allocation inconclusive under power gate.
papers.maturity_note: Useful Route-9 evaluation-integrity evidence for WAM test-time scaling. Scope is one Cosmos Policy/RoboCasa configuration; no author-linked repository, test suite, serving scheduler, admission control, or multi-tenant SLO was verified. Keep WATCH_ONLY; no independent reproduction.

papers.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
papers.system_contribution: Coupling-aware parallel token-commit selection for diffusion language models. Cheap probes are inserted into the main forward pass; the paper reports fewer decoding steps and higher tokens/s than mean-field decoding on one A100, including a KV-cache setting.
papers.maturity_note: Algorithmic decoding contribution, not a serving scheduler/runtime: no admission control, multi-tenant resource management, cache service or serving SLO. Full official PDF reviewed; exact-title GitHub repository search returned no match.

papers.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
papers.system_contribution: La-JEPA is a compact world-action policy trained in V-JEPA 2.1 feature space and generates actions only at inference. The paper reports lower replan latency and 2–5x faster compiled policy calls than Fast-WAM at comparable/better task performance.
papers.maturity_note: Policy/model architecture rather than an inference-serving runtime: no serving scheduler, multi-tenant admission, cache/reuse or fleet SLO. Full official PDF reviewed; exact-title GitHub repository search returned no match.

papers.title: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model
papers.open_source: Author-linked repo verified; inference/evaluation code, data-preparation scripts and checkpoints available; training code and HUGSIM closed-loop evaluation pending.
papers.system_contribution: Offline negative-trajectory supervision and scene-conditioned rider tokens for WAM safety post-training; auxiliary rider branch is removed at inference.
papers.key_results: 40.4 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navhard (+4.1% relative to the strongest compared scorer-free WAM baseline), 93.3 EPDMS on navtest; zero-shot HUGSIM cross-benchmark generalization reported.
papers.maturity_note: Algorithmic WAM safety post-training rather than a serving system; no additional inference-time module or serving scheduler/queueing/concurrency SLO. Keep WATCH_ONLY pending independent reproduction and runtime/SLO evidence.

papers.title: GuidedWAM: Training-Free Energy Guidance for World Action Models in Autonomous Driving
papers.open_source: No exact-name author-linked repository verified.
papers.system_contribution: Jacobian-free energy guidance on the one-step clean estimate of frozen flow-matching WAMs, with sampling-time scheduling, per-energy normalization and velocity-bounded correction.
papers.key_results: Improves three frozen WAMs by 1.8–3.6 EPDMS; guidance adds 1.9 ms to a 36 ms DriveWAM step, 1.4 ms to a 16.3 ms SimWAM step and 0.1 ms to a 48 ms DriveLaW step; under 10% sampling-time overhead.
papers.maturity_note: Inference-time algorithmic control channel, but only open-loop pseudo-simulation on one benchmark and no serving infrastructure, scheduler or concurrency SLO. Keep WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
papers.open_source: No verified author-linked code repository; a same-name UT-Austin-RobIn repository is unverified because it is not linked from the paper page and its README.md lookup returned 404.
papers.system_contribution: Semantic-abduction-based VLA failure correction using dense spatial representations and conditional costs inferred from a small number of corrective demonstrations.
papers.key_results: Evaluated across six manipulation tasks and object/scene variations; abstract reports transfer from a handful of corrective demonstrations.
papers.maturity_note: Policy correction/learning method, not a serving or inference-runtime contribution; no latency or throughput evidence. Keep WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
papers.open_source: No verified author-linked repository; AISG-Group/RM-VLM is a same-name collision whose README describes an unrelated power-operation video action-recognition project.
papers.system_contribution: LLM-generated reward machines from natural-language tasks, VLM proposition grounding on image observations and a VLM-based value-function estimator for dense rewards.
papers.key_results: Evaluated on grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation and 3D object collection; reports higher task success than compared VLM-based reward methods.
papers.maturity_note: RL reward representation and policy-learning method; no serving system, runtime throughput or latency evidence. Keep WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: A Multimodal Haptic Interface for Simultaneous Softness and Thermal Modulation
papers.open_source: No author-linked code repository identified on the official arXiv page.
papers.system_contribution: Tactile display combining particle-jamming stiffness control and heated/cooled-water thermal transfer.
papers.key_results: Prototype reports 300% controllable stiffness increase, 10–50 °C surface temperatures and 0.2 °C closed-loop temperature error.
papers.maturity_note: Physical haptic-interface hardware rather than an AI inference/serving contribution; retain only as adjacent physical-AI hardware context.

papers.title: Introducing Cluster Efficiency to LLM Serving: Pooling Economical Accelerators over Fast Interconnects
papers.open_source: Paper references the Tenstorrent software stack, but a single paper-linked implementation repository, license, and reproducibility package have not yet been independently verified.
papers.system_contribution: A cluster-serving stack pools economical accelerators over fast interconnects using integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay.
papers.key_results: On Tenstorrent Galaxy, 1.07–2.24× tokens per dollar versus an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server under the paper's three-year acquisition-and-electricity model; TCP-class communication emulation reduces throughput by 23.5–67.4%.
papers.maturity_note: 17-page full text validated. Strong serving/resource-pooling contribution; cross-vendor deployment and independent reproduction remain open.

papers.title: Intent-Aware Caching for Efficient LLM Serving
papers.open_source: Paper links an author repository; repository license, test coverage, benchmark reproduction, and production integration still need independent verification.
papers.system_contribution: An online prefix-KV cache eviction policy classifies requests by intent, learns reuse statistics from recent serving logs, and uses predicted continuation probability and inter-turn delay to guide eviction.
papers.key_results: 34.6% cache hit rate versus 18.8% for the previous learning-based policy and 12.2% for LRU; up to 46.1% lower average serving latency on WildChat and ShareChat workloads.
papers.maturity_note: 25-page full text validated. Direct serving-cache contribution with paper-linked code; independent reproduction and SLO/multi-tenant evaluation remain open.

papers.title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation
papers.open_source: Author-linked Lenovo-ICI repository is present in the paper; license, tests, CI, supported backends, and independent reproduction remain to be checked.
papers.system_contribution: A position-independent KV-cache reuse system that selects distribution-aware recomputation to restore cross-chunk interactions while reducing dependence on custom execution flows.
papers.key_results: Full-text evidence confirms serving-oriented KV reuse, recomputation, scheduler, and TTFT analysis; quantitative comparisons require a separate reproduction audit before ranking.
papers.maturity_note: 15-page full text validated. Direct cache/reuse system contribution; backend portability and deployment maturity remain open.

papers.title: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI
papers.open_source: No complete author-linked implementation repository was verified; an extracted GitHub URL was incomplete and is not treated as a valid repo link.
papers.system_contribution: A unified runtime models CNN blocks and Transformer layers as ordered stages and makes budget-aware continue-or-exit decisions from runtime state, inference progress, and predicted latency.
papers.key_results: Full-text review confirms a latency-aware runtime for heterogeneous edge workloads; quantitative deployment results and baseline comparability remain to be extracted in the next evidence pass.
papers.maturity_note: 15-page full text validated. Strong edge-runtime candidate; implementation availability, device diversity, and deadline/SLO reproduction remain open.

papers.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
papers.open_source: Paper links an implementation repository; license, CI/tests, supported GPU generations, and independent reproduction remain open.
papers.system_contribution: Algorithm-system co-design for native FP4 KV-cache decoding, including dual-residual query quantization, underflow-aware probability scaling, outlier-aware key quantization, transposed softmax, and fused probability quantization on paged KV caches.
papers.key_results: On NVIDIA B300 with Qwen3-4B/Qwen3-30B-A3B, 2.4–3.0× peak serving throughput over BF16 KV; accuracy within 0.5 points of BF16 KV with NVFP4 and within 1 point with MXFP4.
papers.maturity_note: 17-page full text validated. High-value KV/precision co-design, but not a serving scheduler or fleet/runtime abstraction; retain SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: MINE: Entropy-coded Memory-efficient Inference for Large Language Models
papers.open_source: Paper states that MINE is open source, but the extracted full text did not expose a direct author repository URL; repository/license verification remains pending.
papers.system_contribution: A GPU entropy-coding inference engine (dtANS-LLM) with per-tensor/per-GPU autotuning, integrated into vLLM as a plugin for memory-bound single-stream decoding.
papers.key_results: On Llama 3.1 8B Instruct with a 2.1-bit EntQuant checkpoint, 2.52× and 1.48× speedups over the fastest baseline on RTX 4060 Ti and RTX 5090 at effective bitrates of 2.24 and 3.43 bits/weight.
papers.maturity_note: 20-page full text validated. Strong memory-efficient inference boundary work; author repository, multi-request behavior, and independent reproduction remain open.

papers.title: ReKV: Overlapping Quantized KV Transfer and Suffix Recomputation
papers.open_source: No author-linked repository was found in the inspected full text.
papers.system_contribution: For prefill–decode disaggregation, transfers a quantized prefix KV cache plus a BF16 boundary state while reconstructing a contiguous suffix on the decode worker, overlapping communication and recomputation.
papers.key_results: In a model-shaped synthetic cross-node H100 benchmark, Q8 reduces 8K handoff latency by 2.36×, 2.84×, and 3.65× for Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-3B, and Qwen3-8B; a separate real-weight BF16 recomputation experiment reduces prefill-to-token-return time by 1.16–1.63×.
papers.maturity_note: 5-page full text validated. Useful disaggregated-serving mechanism, but synthetic transfer benchmark and limited real-weight evidence keep it at SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: TimeOmni-Live: Continuous & Live Time Series Understanding with Long-Term Memory
papers.open_source: No author-linked code repository was identified in the inspected full text.
papers.system_contribution: A continuous time-series model with stream-persistent hybrid memory and elastic stream-inference synchronization for open-ended streams and edge deployment.
papers.key_results: A 4B-parameter model and LiveTS-Suite covering 5K+ streams / 2.2B timesteps; paper reports 206× lower p95 latency than its backbone and Jetson edge deployment.
papers.maturity_note: 46-page full text validated. Relevant streaming/edge inference evidence, but no reusable serving scheduler, multi-tenant isolation, or fleet SLO is established.

papers.title: Atik: A Shared-Mesh Transformer Accelerator for RISC-V
papers.open_source: Paper describes an open-source RoCC accelerator and project website, but a directly verified repository URL and license were not established from the extracted full text.
papers.system_contribution: A shared fixed-point MAC mesh for RocketChip that accelerates matrix multiplication and dense attention with a streaming online-softmax schedule and descriptor-based ABI.
papers.key_results: 137 FireSim test records passed within benchmark tolerance; the 8×8 mesh reports 31.5× peak matmul and 225.8× peak attention speedup versus the scalar Rocket BF16 reference.
papers.maturity_note: 8-page full text validated. Hardware accelerator rather than a serving runtime; retain as SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/WATCH_ONLY.

papers.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.open_source: Paper states that code will be released and links an author repository; repository maturity and license need verification.
papers.system_contribution: Test-time gradient updates encode episode-specific memory into world-model parameters, complementing contextual memory for long-horizon planning.
papers.key_results: Reports state-of-the-art Memory Maze results and preserves performance on DeepMind Control and Atari 100k; no serving/runtime metrics are established.
papers.maturity_note: 34-page full text validated. World-model memory inspiration only; no serving/runtime contribution, so it is not CORE_SYS.

papers.title: Inside the Trap: A Renewal Law for Prefix-Cache Collapse in LLM Agent Serving
papers.open_source: Author-linked public repository verified; MIT license; default branch trap/arxiv at 852600f4674255d886bab31e6ed27d28f937e46f. README reports ~1 GB repository / ~15 GB full checkout and ~1,950 tests; it reports 32 Windows platform-specific test failures. Tests were not independently run in this workspace.
papers.system_contribution: Characterizes a persistent zero-prefix-hit overload trap in agent-serving engines and evaluates client-side session admission caps as a cache-reuse recovery mechanism; includes a fluid FIFO renewal model and real-engine SGLang/vLLM experiments.
papers.key_results: Paper reports 200-session bursts leave zero cache hits through all 30 BURST runs; a session cap prevents the trap in all 30 CAPPED runs and rescues 9/9 established traps without shedding sessions. Registered paired tests span SGLang 0.5.22/vLLM 0.32.0, A100/H200 and Qwen2.5-7B/Llama-3.1-8B.
papers.maturity_note: 66-page full text and official PDF validated. Strong CORE_SYS candidate, but WATCH_ONLY: model F is an idealized all-miss FIFO fluid model and the paper does not prove engine convergence; sessions are synthetic, runs are bounded, and disaggregated serving/larger models/parallelism remain untested. Public MIT repository and test suite verified, but no independent reproduction performed.

papers.title: VLA Handover: Failure-Prediction-Based Switching from On-Robot to Server VLA Models
papers.open_source: No author-linked implementation repository was identified in the inspected full text; the paper cites LeRobot as an upstream base, not as its own artifact.
papers.system_contribution: A selective edge-cloud VLA handover policy: run a small on-robot VLA and invoke a larger server VLA only after a predicted failure alert, reducing per-robot remote inference requests.
papers.key_results: On LIBERO-Object/Goal/Spatial, the paper reports +10.6/+14.7/+22.4 percentage points success over device-only and 77.3%/59.5%/48.5% fewer server requests than server-only, respectively. On LIBERO-Long, success is only 63.6% versus 93.2% server-only and requests are 19.17 versus 29.17 per episode (34.3% fewer); the server is one GB10 at batch 1.
papers.maturity_note: 6-page full text and official PDF validated. SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/WATCH_ONLY: proof-of-concept uses a single server, simulation-only single runs, quasi-static scenes and load-independent light-tailed emulated latency. LIBERO-Long falls to 63.6% versus 93.2% server-only; server selection, load-aware handover, dynamic scenes and real robots remain future work.

papers.title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.open_source: No author-linked repository or license for an implementation was identified in the inspected full text.
papers.system_contribution: Uses the previous action chunk as a geometric prior to prune visual patches before the vision encoder, with separate third-person and wrist-camera policies; this reduces encoder and LLM visual-token work in closed-loop VLA inference.
papers.key_results: On OpenVLA-OFT the paper reports up to 1.61x speedup and 59.5% FLOPs reduction; on pi0.5 the 12.5%-retention setting yields only 1.04x speedup on LIBERO. Four real-robot tasks are reported, but at 50% retention average success is 50% versus 60% vanilla and at 25% retention 37.5%.
papers.maturity_note: 9-page full text and official PDF validated. SYS_ALG_BOUNDARY/WATCH_ONLY: algorithmic token pruning, not a serving runtime/scheduler; gains are backbone-dependent, aggressive pruning harms real-robot success, and calibrated cameras/depth sensing are assumed.

papers.title: FATHOM: World-Model-Guided Diffusion Action-Trajectory Selection for Sparse-Marker AUV Tracking
papers.open_source: No author-linked implementation repository was identified in the inspected full text.
papers.system_contribution: An onboard AUV closed-loop control pipeline combining sparse-marker visual/inertial belief inference, a diffusion action prior, and world-model predictive selection of multi-thruster trajectories.
papers.key_results: On two AUVs in an indoor tank, the follower runs on Jetson AGX Orin at nominal 10 Hz. The paper reports 73.83 ms mean and 85.10 ms P95 inference-plus-selection latency; it completes all 12 challenging trials, reaches 0.163 NRMSE under partial marker visibility, and recovers in all recorded visibility-loss events with 2.17 s mean recovery time.
papers.maturity_note: 18-page full text and official PDF validated. ALG_INSPIRATION/WATCH_ONLY: useful real onboard world-model/diffusion control evidence, but a task-specific AUV controller rather than a general serving runtime; indoor tank, 24 trials/controller, no fleet/tenant isolation or serving SLO. Motion capture supports repeatable leader motion/ground truth but does not feed the follower controller.

papers.title: CascadeRec: Deployed Adaptive LLM Compute Allocation for Multi-Tenant Content Recommendation
papers.open_source: Author-linked offline validation pipeline is public; README declares MIT, but no LICENSE file or CI workflow was found. Production EKS/GKE, vLLM/Bedrock code and tenant data are not released; tests cover ranking metrics only.

papers.key_results: With prefix reuse disabled, repeated runs reproduced every token and reported log-probability in all ten configurations. At Q4_K_M, server-level prompt cache moved run-to-run divergence by 37.5 percentage points under the canonical episode order; five random orders ranged from 20.0% to 28.7%. Restoring cache state made each path internally reproducible while cached and recomputed paths still differed.
papers.maturity_note: Classify CORE_SYS because the reusable cache reproducibility/evaluation harness is directly relevant to serving correctness, cache reuse and quantized inference diagnostics; it is not a new serving runtime or scheduler.
